chapters.1: Hannah, one of Elkanah's two wives, is deeply distressed by her inability to have children and is taunted by the other wife, Peninnah. At the tabernacle in Shiloh, Hannah prays fervently and vows to dedicate a son to God if given one; the priest Eli blesses her, and she conceives and bears a son she names Samuel.
chapters.2: Hannah offers a prayer of praise celebrating God's power to humble the proud and lift up the lowly, then leaves young Samuel to grow up serving at the tabernacle under Eli. The chapter contrasts Samuel's growing faithfulness with the corrupt and abusive behavior of Eli's sons, Hophni and Phinehas, and a prophet warns that Eli's family will lose the priesthood because of their sins.
chapters.3: As a boy serving in the tabernacle, Samuel hears God calling his name at night and, after initially mistaking the voice for Eli's, is told by Eli to respond directly to the Lord. God reveals to Samuel that he will bring judgment on Eli's household, and Samuel begins to be recognized throughout Israel as a true prophet.
chapters.4: Israel suffers a crushing defeat against the Philistines and loses the ark of the covenant, which they had brought into battle in a desperate attempt to secure victory. Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas are both killed, and when Eli hears the news he dies from shock, while his pregnant daughter-in-law names her newborn son Ichabod to mark the loss of God's glory.
chapters.5: The Philistines place the captured ark in the temple of their god Dagon, but the idol is repeatedly found fallen and broken before it. Wherever the ark is taken among Philistine cities, God afflicts the people with a painful plague, making clear that the ark's power cannot be controlled or exploited by Israel's enemies.
chapters.6: After months of suffering, the Philistines consult their priests and decide to send the ark back to Israel along with a guilt offering, testing whether its return on an untended cart pulled by cows confirms it was truly God's doing. The ark arrives safely in Israelite territory, though some men who look into it improperly are struck down.
chapters.7: Samuel calls Israel to abandon idol worship and return fully to the Lord, leading a national gathering at Mizpeh marked by repentance and fasting. When the Philistines attack during this assembly, God intervenes with thunder that routs them, and Samuel sets up a memorial stone called Ebenezer to commemorate God's help.
chapters.8: As Samuel grows old, Israel's elders ask him to appoint a king to rule over them like other nations, which displeases Samuel and grieves God, since it amounts to rejecting the Lord's own kingship. God tells Samuel to grant the request anyway, but first to warn the people clearly about the burdens and costs a king will impose on them.
chapters.9: While searching for his father's lost donkeys, a tall young Benjamite named Saul is led to Samuel, who has been told by God that this man is to be Israel's first king. Samuel treats Saul with special honor at a meal and privately anoints him, though Saul himself has no idea yet what is about to happen.
chapters.10: Samuel anoints Saul as king in private and gives him signs to confirm God's choice, including an encounter with a group of prophesying prophets that causes Saul himself to prophesy. Samuel then presents Saul publicly to Israel by casting lots, and though some doubt this unlikely choice, Saul is confirmed as king at Mizpah.
chapters.11: When the Ammonite king Nahash threatens the city of Jabesh-gilead with a brutal ultimatum, Saul musters Israel's forces and delivers a decisive victory, rescuing the city. This triumph cements popular support for Saul's kingship, and the people formally confirm him as king at Gilgal with celebration and sacrifices.
chapters.12: Samuel delivers a farewell speech as Israel's judge, reviewing his own integrity and reminding the people of God's faithfulness throughout their history despite repeated unfaithfulness. He warns that even with a king now in place, both king and people must still remain obedient to God or face serious consequences.
chapters.13: Saul faces a massive Philistine army at Gilgal, and when Samuel delays in arriving, Saul impatiently offers a sacrifice himself, overstepping his role as king rather than priest. Samuel confronts him for this disobedience and declares that Saul's kingship will not continue in his family line, while noting that Israel's army is poorly armed compared to the Philistines.
chapters.14: Jonathan, Saul's son, boldly attacks a Philistine outpost with just his armor-bearer, trusting that God can grant victory regardless of numbers, and this triggers a panic that leads to a larger Israelite victory. Saul later nearly has Jonathan executed for unknowingly breaking a food-related vow made during the battle, but the army intervenes to save him.
chapters.15: God commands Saul to completely destroy the Amalekites and all their possessions as judgment for past hostility toward Israel, but Saul disobeys by sparing their king Agag and the best livestock. Samuel confronts Saul, declaring that obedience matters more than sacrifice, and announces that God has rejected Saul as king because of his disobedience.
chapters.16: God sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint one of Jesse's sons as the next king, and rather than choosing an impressive-looking older son, God selects the youngest, David, a shepherd, emphasizing that God looks at the heart rather than outward appearance. David also begins serving in Saul's court, playing the harp to soothe Saul when he is troubled by a tormenting spirit.
chapters.17: The Philistine giant Goliath challenges Israel to send a champion to fight him, and while Saul's army is terrified, the young shepherd David volunteers, trusting in God's past deliverances. Armed only with a sling and stones, David kills Goliath, leading to a rout of the Philistine army and David's rise to national fame.
chapters.18: David's great popularity after defeating Goliath, along with his close friendship with Saul's son Jonathan, begins to provoke Saul's jealousy and fear that David will take his throne. Saul tries several schemes to have David killed or discredited, including dangerous military assignments, but David continues to succeed and marries Saul's daughter Michal.
chapters.19: Saul's jealousy toward David intensifies into open attempts on his life, including throwing a spear at him, but Jonathan and Michal both help protect David from their father. David eventually has to flee for his life to Samuel at Ramah, where Saul's pursuing men are overcome by a prophetic frenzy.
chapters.20: David and Jonathan reaffirm their deep friendship and devise a secret signal system to let David know whether it's safe to return, since Jonathan still hopes to reconcile his father to David. When Saul's anger at a feast confirms his murderous intent, Jonathan warns David to flee, and the two friends part in sorrow, renewing their covenant of loyalty.
chapters.21: On the run from Saul, David goes to the priest Ahimelech at Nob, deceiving him about his mission in order to get food and a weapon, taking the sword of Goliath. David then flees to the Philistine city of Gath, where he pretends to be insane to avoid being recognized and killed by King Achish.
chapters.22: David gathers a band of followers, including family members and others in distress, while hiding in the cave of Adullam and later in Moab. Saul, enraged that the priest Ahimelech helped David, orders the massacre of the priests of Nob and their families, though one son, Abiathar, escapes to join David.
chapters.23: David rescues the town of Keilah from a Philistine raid, using guidance from God through the priest Abiathar to know when to move and avoid Saul's pursuit. Saul continues hunting David through the wilderness of Ziph, but Jonathan secretly meets David to renew their covenant, and Saul is eventually called away before capturing him.
chapters.24: While pursuing David in the wilderness of Engedi, Saul unknowingly enters the very cave where David and his men are hiding, giving David a chance to kill him. David instead only cuts a piece of Saul's robe and later confronts Saul from a distance, showing he spared the king's life out of respect for God's anointed, which moves Saul to acknowledge David's righteousness.
chapters.25: After Samuel's death, David sends a respectful request for provisions to the wealthy but foolish Nabal, who insults David's men and refuses to help despite their past kindness to him. Nabal's wise wife Abigail intervenes with gifts and diplomacy to prevent bloodshed, and after Nabal dies suddenly, David marries Abigail.
chapters.26: Saul again pursues David into the wilderness of Ziph, and David sneaks into Saul's camp at night with Abishai, taking Saul's spear and water jug as proof he could have killed him but chose not to. From a safe distance, David again confronts Saul about his unjust pursuit, and Saul once more admits his wrongdoing, though the two part without lasting reconciliation.
chapters.27: Weary of Saul's relentless pursuit, David takes refuge among the Philistines, settling in the town of Ziklag under King Achish's protection. From there David raids various raiding peoples while deceiving Achish about who he is actually attacking, maintaining his position among the Philistines without betraying Israel.
chapters.28: As the Philistines prepare for a major battle against Israel, Saul, desperate for guidance since God has gone silent toward him, visits a medium at Endor despite having outlawed such practices. The spirit of Samuel appears and delivers a grim prophecy that Saul and his sons will die and Israel will be defeated the next day.
chapters.29: David, now living among the Philistines, is prepared to march to battle alongside King Achish against Israel, but the Philistine commanders distrust him and insist he be sent away rather than risk his loyalty switching mid-battle. Achish reluctantly agrees, sparing David from having to fight against his own people.
chapters.30: While David and his men are away, Amalekite raiders attack and burn their town of Ziklag, carrying off the women and children, including David's own wives. With God's guidance, David pursues the raiders, rescues all the captives, and generously shares the recovered plunder, even with those who had been too exhausted to join the chase.
chapters.31: In the climactic battle against the Philistines on Mount Gilboa, Saul's sons are killed and Saul himself, badly wounded, falls on his own sword to avoid capture, with his armor-bearer following suit. The Philistines display Saul's body in triumph, but the men of Jabesh-gilead honor him by recovering and properly burying his remains.
